newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate jumps to 11.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate jumps to 11.2 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate, boosted by the higher price of call money placements, jumped to 11.2 percent on Monday from Friday's 9.4 percent.
Dealers put total trade at 30.8 million kuna of which only 7.0 million were new funds, against 90 million kuna in supply.
Old call money loans, rolled over at higher prices than the recent 9.0 percent, pushed the weighted rate to 10.25 percent.
Term rates ranged from 8.0 percent, charged by insurers for one-week funds, to 18 percent for one-month bank borrowings.
Overnight settlements at the weekend totalled a mere 0.28 million kuna as only one bank had a shortfall to cover.

The central bank stayed out of the foreign exchange market and calculated the kuna midrates for Tuesday stronger at 5.3685 to the dollar but slightly weaker at 3.5690 against the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
